lede: Gold ended the week about 3% lower at its weakest close of the year as December Fed hike bets and higher oil hit demand; tech earnings dragged the Nasdaq down 2%. Forex and gold reopen on Monday, while crypto trades quietly as Binance begins reopening withdrawals today.

focus.text: Closed Friday near $3,875, the lowest close of 2026, after oil-driven inflation fears outweighed safe-haven demand. It sits below Monday's pivot of 3,924.5; US ISM data opens the week.
Lost about 0.4% on the week to 1.1157, holding just above the 1.1100 support area. Wednesday's eurozone flash CPI and Friday's US payrolls are the week's main tests.

technicals.indicators: RSI(14) ≈ 30, oversold · below 50/100/200-day MAs · MACD bearish
technicals.note: Lower highs and lower lows since the August peak near $4,700. Price is now testing the 3,850–3,880 support zone.

technicals.indicators: Short-term neutral after the rebound from 1.1103
technicals.note: The larger decline from 1.2081 stays in place while 1.1269 holds; a break below 1.1100 would extend it toward the 61.8% retracement.

technicals.indicators: Below 50-day MA (~81,900) · above 200-day MA (~73,100) · daily RSI mid-30s
technicals.note: Holding just above last week's six-week low after the Binance hack; the range has narrowed to roughly 77,000–77,700 over the weekend with no confirmed reversal signal.

technicals.indicators: RSI near the bottom of its neutral range
technicals.note: Fell on heavy volume; holding the 2,170–2,200 area is the first test.

news.text: Seven core OPEC+ members meet online today; sources point to unchanged December output targets, and the result will shape Monday's oil open.
Brent finished October up about 13.6%, its fourth straight monthly gain, after mines were found on a tanker near the Strait of Hormuz.
Two Fed officials dissented in favour of a hike at last week's hold, and strong Q3 growth of 3.4% kept December tightening bets alive.
The S&P 500 slipped 0.6% for a third weekly loss as Alphabet and Intel results weighed on mega-cap tech; health care led sectors.
Sterling edged up on the week as markets almost fully price a Bank of England hike on Thursday.
Binance says it has replaced 90% of the roughly $6.3B stolen in last week's hack and plans to reopen withdrawals in phases from today.
A first proof-of-reserves snapshot showed full coverage by Binance's own account; a full zero-knowledge proof is due around 3 Nov. CertiK wants more detail.
Around 7,499 BTC, worth about $580M, moved from Binance's SAFU fund wallet to an unidentified address on Saturday.
Hyperliquid's token jumped about 15% on the week after ICE agreed to run Hyperliquid-based perpetual futures for US users.
Ripple won final OCC approval to set up a US national trust bank.
Strive added 6,182 BTC for more than $510M, its biggest purchase so far.

upcoming.note: Sources expect December targets to stay unchanged.
About 79% priced for a 25bp hike to 4.85%.
All 435 House seats and 35 Senate seats; results overnight into Wednesday.
Binance says the proof takes 40–50 hours to generate.
Consensus +55k, unemployment 4.2%. US clocks changed, so it is 16:30 TRT.

weekly_summary.summary: A hawkish Fed hold, with two officials voting to hike, and strong US growth and inflation data revived bets on a December rate rise. Oil climbed after attacks on shipping near Hormuz, which fed inflation worries and pushed gold to its lowest close of the year instead of lifting it as a haven. Disappointing tech earnings pulled the Nasdaq down 2%, and crypto was hit by the record $6.3B Binance hack. The dollar was mixed: the euro slipped while sterling firmed on Bank of England hike bets.

performance.note: Rate-hike bets, oil-led inflation fears, ETF outflows
Third weekly loss; Alphabet and Intel weighed

top_stories.text: The Fed held at 3.75–4.00% but two dissenters backed a hike, lifting December hike odds.
Gold dropped over 3.6% on Friday to its lowest close of 2026; silver lost nearly 9% on the week and fell below $50.
Binance suffered a roughly $6.3B hack linked to North Korea; about $3B was frozen and the exchange pledged to cover users.
A mined tanker near Hormuz pushed Brent above $113; oil gained about 13.6% in October.
Alphabet fell about 12% and Intel nearly 29% after results, raising doubts over the payoff from AI spending.
US Q3 GDP grew 3.4% and core PCE inflation ran at 3.1%, keeping pressure on the Fed.
